rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If a transformed human either perished and a new pig was created, or persisted while its bodily structure changed, the human is distinct from the body.
rows.anchor: إن ذلك الإنسان هل بقي حال ذلك المسخ أو لم يبق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel and Satan could appear in human form without being human in essence, so the human is not identical with the visible bodily form.
rows.anchor: كان يرى جبريل عليه الصلاة والسلام في صورة دحية الكلبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In adultery the sexual organ acts while the back receives punishment; the experiencing subject is distinct from both organs.
rows.anchor: أن الزاني يزني بفرجه فيضرب على ظهره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The addressee of commands is no particular body part; identifying it with the whole body also fails, since one cognition cannot inhabit many parts and each part is not independently knowing.
rows.anchor: المخاطب بهذا الخطاب والمأمور والمنهي ليس هو جبهة زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Free choice requires knowledge, which Razi locates in the heart by introspection and scripture; therefore the human subject is something in the heart, not the bodily frame.
rows.anchor: العلم لا يحصل إلا في القلب فيلزم أن يكون الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since a human essence is neither surface nor color, while everything visible is one of those, the human essence is not visible or otherwise sensible.
rows.anchor: حقيقة الإنسان شيء مغاير للسطح واللون وكل ما هو مرئي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A bodily candidate within a human must be a mixture of the four elements; no pure elemental body occurs in the body.
rows.anchor: لا بد وأن يكون الحاصل جسما متولدا من امتزاجات هذه الأربعة

rows.speaker: القائلون بأن الإنسان شيء مغاير لهذا الجسد
rows.claim: No proponent who distinguishes the human from the body identifies the person with a dense earthy organ such as bone, nerve, flesh, or skin.
rows.anchor: لم يقل أحد من العقلاء بأن الإنسان عبارة عن أحد هذه الأعضاء

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Among the humors, some identify the human spirit with blood because its departure entails death.
rows.anchor: إلا في الدم فإن منهم من قال إنه هو الروح بدليل أنه إذا خرج

rows.speaker: منهم من يقول
rows.claim: One bodily theory identifies the human with airy spirits mixed with innate heat, generated either in the heart or brain.
rows.anchor: أجسام هوائية مخلوطة بالحرارة الغريزية متولدة إما في القلب أو في الدماغ

rows.speaker: منهم من يقول
rows.claim: One view locates the human spirit in the heart; another makes it an indivisible part in the brain.
rows.anchor: فمنهم من يقول الإنسان هو الروح الذي في القلب

rows.speaker: من الناس
rows.claim: Another view makes the person the fiery innate heat mixed with the cardiac and cerebral spirits.
rows.anchor: الروح عبارة عن أجزاء نارية مختلطة بهذه الأرواح القلبية والدماغية

rows.speaker: من الناس
rows.claim: Razi calls worthy of reflection a theory of imperishable, luminous celestial bodies entering the prepared body like oil in sesame; thick humors later block them and cause death.
rows.anchor: فهذا مذهب قوي شريف يجب التأمل فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi knows of no one who says the human is a body located outside the body.
rows.anchor: وأما أن الإنسان جسم موجود خارج البدن فلا أعرف أحدا ذهب إلى هذا القول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human cannot be an accident in the body: the human is a substance described by knowledge, power, deliberation, and action.
rows.anchor: من المعلوم بالضرورة أن الإنسان جوهر لأنه موصوف بالعلم والقدرة

rows.speaker: جمهور الأطباء ومنكري بقاء النفس وأبو الحسين البصري
rows.claim: Humanity is a particular mixture of elemental bodies and temperament, just as other mixture-ranges yield other species; its advocates include most physicians, deniers of soul-survival, and Abu al-Husayn al-Basri.
rows.anchor: هذا قول جمهور الأطباء ومنكري بقاء النفس وقول أبي الحسين البصري

rows.speaker: أكثر شيوخ المعتزلة
rows.claim: Most early Mu'tazilite authorities deny a separate soul and define the human as bodies bearing life, knowledge, and power.
rows.anchor: وهذا مذهب أكثر شيوخ المعتزلة

rows.speaker: القائلون بهذا القول
rows.claim: A view distinguishes humans from animals by bodily shape, but Razi rejects it: angels can assume human forms and transformed humans retain humanity without that form.
rows.anchor: فقد بطل اعتبار هذا الشكل في حصول معنى الإنسانية طردا وعكسا

rows.speaker: أكثر الإلهيين من الفلاسفة
rows.claim: Most philosophers affirm an immaterial soul that survives for spiritual resurrection, reward, punishment, and reckoning; Razi also names al-Raghib, al-Ghazali, Mu'ammar b. 'Abbad, al-Mufid, and some Karramites.
rows.anchor: وذهب إليه جماعة عظيمة من علماء المسلمين مثل الشيخ أبي القاسم الراغب الأصفهاني والشيخ أبي حامد الغزالي

rows.speaker: المحققون
rows.claim: The investigators identify the human with a particular immaterial substance, neither inside nor outside the world, related to the body through governance and direction.
rows.anchor: الإنسان عبارة عن هذا الجوهر المخصوص ، وهذا البدن

rows.speaker: الفريق الثاني
rows.claim: A second soul theory says soul and body unite into the human; at death the union ends, the body decays, and the soul remains.
rows.anchor: فصارت النفس عين البدن ، والبدن عين النفس

rows.speaker: ثابت بن قرة
rows.claim: Thabit ibn Qurra says the soul is connected to subtle, luminous celestial bodies that permeate the body and leave it at death.
rows.anchor: وكان ثابت بن قرة يثبت النفس ويقول إنها متعلقة بأجسام سماوية نورانية لطيفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the human substance occupied space, spatial extension would be essential to it; yet one knows oneself without conceiving extension, so the human is not a spatial body.
rows.anchor: أنا قد نعرف ذاتنا حال كوننا جاهلين بالتحيز والامتداد في الجهات الثلاثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Against the objection that self-knowledge should reveal an immaterial nature, Razi answers that being nonspatial is a negative property, not the known essence itself.
rows.anchor: كونه مجردا معناه أنه ليس بمتحيز ولا حالا في المتحيز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The self signified by each person's I is immediately known to be one, though this alone does not decide whether it is internally composite.
rows.anchor: كان ذلك المشار إليه واحدا غير متعدد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anger and desire require awareness of what is harmful or pleasing, so the subject who responds must itself perceive.
rows.anchor: فالذي يغضب لا بد وأن يكون هو بعينه مدركا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If perception, anger, and desire belonged to independent substances, engaging one would not impede another; since they do interfere, they are states of one substance.
rows.anchor: فعلمنا أن هذه الأمور الثلاثة ليست مباديء مستقلة بل هي صفات مختلفة بجوهر واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When perception causes desire or anger, the perceiver must be the very same subject that desires and becomes angry.
rows.anchor: صاحب الإدراك بعينه هو صاحب الشهوة بعينها وصاحب الغضب بعينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because voluntary movement requires awareness of good and harm, one human soul is the subject of all senses, imagination, thought, memory, desire, anger, and voluntary action.
rows.anchor: أن النفس الإنسانية شيء واحد وثبت أن ذلك الشيء هو المبصر والسامع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The soul is not the entire body or a bodily part: capacities such as sight and hearing are assigned to particular organs, and no one part bears every perception and action.
rows.anchor: ليس في البدن جزء واحد وهو بعينه موصوف بالأبصار والسماع والفكر والذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeing, knowing, desiring, and moving toward an object belong to one subject; assigning them to different subjects breaks the causal sequence.
rows.anchor: الذي أبصر هو الذي عرف وأن الذي عرف هو الذي اشتهى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Speech likewise requires one agent to understand and intend meaning, produce sounds through vocal organs, and move the body; this unified agent is distinct from the various organs.
rows.anchor: محل العلوم والإرادات هو القلب لزم أيضا أن يكون محل الصوت هو القلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The organs are instruments: the distinct soul sees with the eye, hears with the ear, thinks with the brain, and reasons with the heart, governing the body.
rows.anchor: والنفس جوهر مغاير لها مفارق عنها بالذات متعلق بها تعلق التصرف والتدبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If life and knowledge belonged separately to every bodily part, one body would contain many independent humans who might will conflicting movements; if one property belonged to all parts, one accident would occupy many substrates.
rows.anchor: والقسمان باطلان فبطل القول بكون الإنسان عبارة عن هذا الجسد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proposed fix that life in one part makes the whole body alive fails: a single property across the whole body is impossible, while separate properties make many humans.
rows.anchor: إن حصل في مجموع جثة مجموع حياة واحدة وعالمية واحدة فقد حصلت الصفة الواحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike material forms, which replace one another, acquired intelligible forms make further learning easier and accumulate without weakening the soul.
rows.anchor: ثم إن النفس لا تزال تقبل صورة بعد صورة من غير أن تضعف ألبتة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Careful thought perfects the soul but dries and weakens the body; one entity cannot thereby be perfected and damaged, alive and dying, at once.
rows.anchor: هذه الأفكار توجب حياة النفس وشرفها وتوجب نقصان البدن وموته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A weak body can become fearless and powerful when sacred light or a hidden divine mystery appears to the person, indicating a distinct soul.
rows.anchor: فإذا لاح له نور من الأنوار القدسية وتجلى له سر من أسرار عالم الغيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ascetic discipline weakens bodily powers while strengthening spiritual powers and divine knowledge; indulgence instead leaves a person beastlike and without reason.
rows.anchor: كلما أمعنوا في قهر القوى البدنية وتجويع الجسد قويت قواهم الروحانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The soul uses organs for sensation and movement, yet retains knowledge without bodily instruments; closing eyes or ears blocks sight or hearing, not what one already knows.
rows.anchor: لا يمكنه البتة أن يزيل عن قلبه العلم بما كان عالما به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forgetting oneself in ignorance cannot mean forgetting the visible body, so the self mentioned in the verse is other than the body.
rows.anchor: أن أحدا من العقلاء لا ينسى هذا الهيكل المشاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to bring forth the selves is explicit evidence that the self differs from the body.
rows.anchor: وهذا صريح أن النفس غير البدن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stages through which the body develops differ from the subsequent breathing of spirit; the objection that humans are part of clay fails because min marks origin, not composition.
rows.anchor: من التغيرات الواقعة في الأحوال الجسمانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God distinguishes bodily fashioning from breathing His spirit and attributes the spirit to Himself, showing that spirit and body have different essences.
rows.anchor: ميز تعالى بين البشرية وبين نفخ الروح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The soul is one subject capable of cognition and action, whereas neither the whole body nor a bodily part bears both descriptions; the verse supports a distinct substance.
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية صريحة في وجود شيء موصوف بالإدراك والتحريك حقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The single human tested by divine duties and described as hearing and seeing cannot be the body as a whole or any one part, so the soul differs from both.
rows.anchor: فهذا تصريح بأن الإنسان شيء واحد وذلك الشيء هو المبتلي بالتكاليف الإلهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Numerous reports about souls before embodiment and after bodily separation also show that the soul is distinct from the body.
rows.anchor: الأحاديث الواردة في صفة الأرواح قبل تعلقها بالأجساد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi calls it astonishing that someone can read these verses and reports yet claim the Prophet died without knowing the spirit.
rows.anchor: ثم يقول توفى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وما كان يعرف الروح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If spirit were a body progressing through states, the answer would describe its formation as it does the body's; calling it from God's command and created by Be instead identifies it as a holy, immaterial substance.
rows.anchor: دل ذلك على أنه جوهر ليس من جنس الأجسام بل هو جوهر قدسي مجرد

rows.speaker: الواسطي
rows.claim: Al-Wasiti reports that God created spirits from beauty and radiance; if their glory were unveiled, every disbeliever would prostrate.
rows.anchor: قال الواسطي : خلق الله الأرواح من بين الجمال والبهاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spirit first relates to the heart, then its influence reaches all bodily members, as Razi explained under the verse about the Trustworthy Spirit.
rows.anchor: أن تعلقه الأول بالقلب ثم بواسطته يصل تأثيره إلى جملة الأعضاء

rows.speaker: المنكرون
rows.claim: Opponents argue that a nonbodily, nonaccidental soul would match God's essence; Razi replies that sharing a negative property does not entail likeness or identity.
rows.anchor: المساواة في أنه ليس بمتحيز ولا حال في المتحيز مساواة في صفة سلبية

rows.speaker: المنكرون
rows.claim: Opponents cite the human created from a drop, dying and buried, as proof that the human is the body; Razi answers that ordinary usage calls the body the human.
rows.anchor: لما كان الإنسان في العرف والظاهر عبارة عن هذه الجثة أطلق عليه اسم الإنسان

rows.speaker: المنكرون
rows.claim: Opponents say the provision and joy promised to slain believers are bodily qualities; Razi says this provision is knowledge and love of God, while their buried bodies and spirits beneath the Throne demonstrate the soul's difference.
rows.anchor: وهذا يدل على أن الروح غير البدن وليكن هذا آخر كلامنا في هذا الباب

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Exegetes report that listeners asked whether the Prophet alone had little knowledge; he replied that both they and he had received little, prompting their comparison with the promise of abundant good.
rows.anchor: بل نحن وأنتم لم نؤت من العلم إلا قليلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no contradiction: human knowledge is little beside God's knowledge and the realities of things, yet abundant beside bodily desires and pleasures.
rows.anchor: فالعلوم الحاصلة عند الناس قليلة جدا بالنسبة إلى علم الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After granting people little knowledge, God says He could remove even that by erasing its memory from hearts and its written traces from books, despite this being extraordinary.
rows.anchor: يمحو حفظه من القلوب وكتابته من الكتب

rows.speaker: الكعبي
rows.claim: Al-Ka'bi argues that the Quran is created because anything God can remove cannot be eternal.
rows.anchor: احتج الكعبي بهذه الآية على أن القرآن مخلوق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi calls that inference remote: removing knowledge from hearts and inscriptions from manuscripts does not show that the known or signified Quran is created.
rows.anchor: وذلك لا يوجب كون ذلك المعلوم المدلول محدثا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about finding no agent means there would be no one to rely on to restore any part of the revelation.
rows.anchor: أي لا تجد من تتوكل عليه في رد شيء منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Except by mercy means either that God may mercifully return the revelation, or, as a disconnected exception, that His mercy left it unerased; its preservation is divine favor.
rows.anchor: إلا أن يرحمك ربك فيرده عليك أو يكون على الاستثناء المنقطع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's favor to scholars includes two gifts: making knowledge accessible and preserving it in them.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : تسهيل ذلك العلم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation says God's great favor is preserving knowledge and Quran for the Prophet.
rows.anchor: المراد أن فضله كان عليك كبيرا بسبب إبقاء العلم والقرآن عليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second interpretation locates the great favor in making Muhammad master of Adam's children, the seal of prophets, and possessor of the Praiseworthy Station.
rows.anchor: جعلك سيد ولد آدم وختم بك النبيين وأعطاك المقام المحمود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People explain Quranic inimitability either by its intrinsic character or by God's diversion of opponents despite their strong motives to compose a rival.
rows.anchor: القرآن في نفسه إما أن يكون معجزا أو لا يكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi's argument is a dilemma: if the Quran is intrinsically inimitable, the claim is established; otherwise motivated opponents had means and no hindrance, so their failure itself breaks the norm and is miraculous.
rows.anchor: فعدم الإتيان بهذه المعارضة مع التقديرات المذكورة يكون نقضا للعادة

rows.speaker: العلماء
rows.claim: Against the question whether human incapacity proves jinn incapacity, scholars answer that human failure alone suffices to establish the Quran's miracle.
rows.anchor: بأن عجز البشر عن معارضته يكفي في إثبات كونه معجزا

rows.speaker: العلماء
rows.claim: Against the suggestion that jinn composed the Quran and gave it to Muhammad, scholars argue God would expose such deception; the final verses of al-Shu'ara also answer it.
rows.anchor: لوجب في حكمة الله أن يظهر ذلك التلبيس وحيث لم يظهر ذلك دل على عدمه

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Mu'tazilites argue that the challenge treats the Quran as something created, since challenging with an eternal thing would be impossible; Razi notes this was addressed at length in al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: قالت المعتزلة الآية دالة على أن القرآن مخلوق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Diversifying examples may mean presenting the challenge at several levels: the whole Quran, ten surahs, one surah, or even one discourse; refusal after failure shows persistence in disbelief.
rows.anchor: وقع التحدي بكل القرآن كما في هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The examples may instead recount how Noah's people, 'Ad, and Thamud suffered different punishments, without persuading the people of Mecca.
rows.anchor: الذين بقوا مصرين على الكفر مثل قوم نوح وعاد وثمود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third reading is that the Quran repeatedly gives proofs of divine unity, answers objections to prophethood and resurrection, and still fails to move the disbelievers.
rows.anchor: ذكر دلائل التوحيد ونفي الشركاء والأضداد في هذا القرآن مرارا كثيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here most people means the people of Mecca, and kufur means denial of truth; the syntax is valid because aba itself conveys negation, meaning they accepted nothing but denial.
rows.anchor: لفظ أبى يفيد النفي كأنه قيل فلم يرضوا إلا كفورا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran's miracle corresponding to Muhammad's claim completes the proof of his prophethood; repeated demands for further miracles would let obstinate people prolong challenges without end.
rows.anchor: فحينئذ تم الدليل على كونه نبيا صادقا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Meccan leaders requested six signs: a spring, a garden with rivers, a gold house, the sky falling in pieces, ascent by ladder, and angels witnessing; Muhammad said he could not provide them.
rows.anchor: فهذا شرح هذه القصة كما رواها ابن عباس

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن أمية المخزومي
rows.claim: Abd Allah ibn Umayya demanded a ladder to heaven and four angel witnesses, while admitting he still might not believe afterward.
rows.anchor: لا أومن بك حتى تشد سلما فتصعد فيه ونحن ننظر إليك

rows.speaker: عاصم وحمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: These readers pronounce tafjura lightly here; Abu Hatim prefers the light form because yanbuʿ is singular, while the others read it with doubling, preferred by Abu Ubayda.
rows.anchor: قرأ عاصم وحمزة والكسائي تفجر بفتح التاء وسكون الفاء

rows.speaker: القراء
rows.claim: All readers use the doubled form for the second verb because rivers are plural; doubling can also express repeated or abundant flow from a single spring.
rows.anchor: ولم يختلفوا في الثانية مشددة لأجل الأنهار

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra explains yanbuʿ as a spring from which water wells up; the Meccans wanted mountains removed and a spring to make cultivation easier.
rows.anchor: يعني : عينا ينبع الماء منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their demand for a garden and rivers can mean: if you will not open rivers for us, then open them for your own sake.
rows.anchor: هب أنك لا تفجر هذه الأنهار لأجلنا ففجرها من أجلك

rows.speaker: ابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn Amir reads kasafan with a fatḥa on sin here and everywhere in the Quran.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر كسفا بفتح السين ها هنا وفي سائر القرآن

rows.speaker: نافع وأبو بكر عن عاصم
rows.claim: Nafi and Abu Bakr from Asim read kasafan with a fatḥa here and in al-Rum, but with sukūn elsewhere.
rows.anchor: قرأ نافع وأبو بكر عن عاصم

rows.speaker: حفص
rows.claim: Hafs reads kasafan with a fatḥa throughout the Quran except in al-Rum.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حفص في سائر القرآن بالفتح إلا في الروم

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وحمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: These readers use a fatḥa in al-Rum and sukūn in the remaining Quranic occurrences.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وحمزة والكسائي

rows.speaker: أبو زيد والليث والفراء
rows.claim: The lexicographers gloss kasf as a cut piece: Abu Zayd uses cutting cloth, al-Layth a severed tendon or fragment, and al-Farra cites an Arab requesting a piece.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء : سمعت أعرابيا يقول لبزاز : أعطني كسفة

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: With sukūn, kasaf may be a plural of kasfa, like damna/diman or sidra/sidr.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء أن يكون جمع كسفة

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: If kasf is a verbal noun, it means a cut object, as in grinding, cooking, and watering; the falling fragment in al-Tur supports this.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي : إذا كان المصدر الكسف

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Zajjaj derives the form from covering and interprets it as a layer falling over them; with fatḥa, kasaf is a plural of kasfa, a fragmented sky used adverbially.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج : من قرأ : كسفا كأنه قال أو يسقطها طبقا علينا

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima reads as you claimed to mean: you claim to be a prophet, Muhammad, so make the sky fall on us.
rows.anchor: قال عكرمة كما زعمت يا محمد أنك نبي فأسقط السماء علينا

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Others understand as you claimed to mean that Muhammad claimed his Lord could act if He willed.
rows.anchor: قال آخرون كما زعمت أن ربك إن شاء فعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third interpretation links their words to the threat in this surah: they ask him to make the sky fall like hailstones upon them.
rows.anchor: أن يخسف بكم جانب البر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qibalan may mean face to face or opposite, like ʿashir for one who associates; this exposes their ignorance in imagining God can confront them bodily.
rows.anchor: القبيل بمعنى المقابل كالعشير بمعنى المعاشر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses qibalan as groups arriving one after another; al-Layth says any troop of jinn or humans is a qabil.
rows.anchor: ما قاله ابن عباس يريد فوجا

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Zajjaj takes qibalan to mean guarantors or sureties; the singular form may refer to a plural, as in good companions.
rows.anchor: إن قوله قبيلا معناه ها هنا ضامنا وكفيلا

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali interprets qibalan as visible in person, supported by the demand elsewhere to see God.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي معناه المعاينة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the companions did not know what zukhruf meant until seeing Abd Allah's reading, a house of gold.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد : كنا لا ندري ما الزخرف

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Zajjaj explains zukhruf as ornament or adornment and links it to the earth taking on its full decoration.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج : الزخرف الزينة

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra gives the verb forms raqiya, arqa, raqyun, and ruqiyyan for ascending; the cited poet, unnamed here, uses ruqiy for climbing stairs.
rows.anchor: أنت الذي كلفتني رقي الدرج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the sky means into the sky's ascents, with the genitive complement omitted; Arabic likewise says one climbs a ladder or step.
rows.anchor: وقوله في السماء أي في معارج السماء فحذف المضاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They say they will not believe because of Muhammad's ascent until he descends with a written book from heaven confirming him.
rows.anchor: أي لن نؤمن لأجل رقيك

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن أمية
rows.claim: Abd Allah ibn Umayya demanded that a ladder be built to heaven, Muhammad ascend while he watched, and return with an open document and four angel witnesses.
rows.anchor: حتى تأتيها ثم تأتي معك بصك منشور معه أربعة من الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The quoted unbelievers' words appear in the same Quranic composition, prompting the objection that people could produce comparable speech.
rows.anchor: وإنا لا نجد بين تلك الكلمات وبين سائر آيات القرآن تفاوتا في النظم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi answers that this brief passage cannot display the difference among levels of eloquence, so the objection fails.
rows.anchor: أن هذا القرآن قليل لا يظهر فيه التفاوت بين مراتب الفصاحة والبلاغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Subhana Rabbi declares God above coming and going; Razi takes it as a rejection of the request that God appear, against anthropomorphists.
rows.anchor: عن الإتيان والمجيء وذلك يدل على فساد قول المشبهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is not about controlling demands upon God, since the Meccans asked the Prophet to seek signs and thus directed their demand at him.
rows.anchor: فالقوم تحكموا على الرسول وما تحكموا على الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the demand was for Muhammad to produce the signs himself, it fails because he is human and humans cannot perform them.
rows.anchor: والأول باطل لأني بشر والبشر لا قدرة له على هذه الأشياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they wanted him to ask God for signs, that is needless after the Quran's proof of his mission and amounts to obstinacy and control.
rows.anchor: والثاني أيضا باطل لأني قد أتيتكم بمعجزة واحدة وهي القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As God's commanded servant, Muhammad cannot control God; his answer is sufficient.
rows.anchor: وأنا عبد مأمور ليس لي أن أتحكم على الله فسقط هذا السؤال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi concludes that the challengers err about divinity and prophethood: God does not move, and Muhammad is a human messenger.
rows.anchor: كونهم على الضلال في الإلهيات ، وفي النبوات
